title: Timpani
reference_instrument: VCSL Timpani 2B one-shots, hits, velocity layers v2 to v5 (Versilian Community Sample Library, CC0); VCSL documents nothing about the drum, so the card is a measured drum of the same class, Fleischer's Kolberg Pauke Nr. 2 with kettle B, tuned to the recordings' principal
summary: A 4 s strike of kettle B at 288 kHz. Its partial ratios match the model's own coupled modes within 0.3 %. The decay is measured, not graded. Its T60s are 1.93 s for (1,1), 2.07 for (2,1), 2.50 for (3,1), 2.43 for (4,1) and 1.6 to 1.84 for (5,1). The VCSL Timpani 2B recordings give 1.3 to 2.3 s for (1,1) and 8.2 to 9.1 for (2,1) on all six hits, and at layers v3 and v5 they give 10 to 11 for (3,1), about 10 for (4,1) and about 7 for (5,1). These T60s bound this model only, not the drum: with head loss at zero, the render's upper partials still decay about 4 times faster than the recording's. VCSL documents nothing about its drum and it is not this one, so the recording locates a defect and sets no target. Nothing is tuned to it, and a fix has to come from the fit or the formulation
physics_present: Head: a tensioned 0.2 mm PET film (Remo Weather King thickness, DuPont Mylar constants) with bending and nonlinear stretching, on Fleischer's measured kettle B (bearing-edge radius 357 mm, 140 l); 17 modes up to the (5,1) pair

Interior air: the kettle's own pressure modes, every angular order, up to 1500 Hz (68 modes), coupled to the head by reciprocal pressure work, so the bulk compliance raises the (0,1) and the interior air's near-field mass lowers every mode

Exterior air: a closed-surface BEM of the head and the kettle's outer wall from 40 to 400 Hz, kept as its reciprocal part and fitted to a 272-pole passive multiport load whose radiation damping and added mass act inside the same time step
Mallet: Rhaouti, Chaigne and Joly's measured timpani mallet (0.028 kg effective mass, F = 1.6e8 x^2.54, 1.4 m/s, contact window from ink spots), struck 10 cm in from the rim
Tension: computed (2582 N/m) so the coupled (1,1) mode sits at the 2B recordings' principal (112.1 Hz); every other frequency follows from the physics
Receiver: the BEM's own pressure 1 m off the axis and 1 m above the head plane, in free field
physics_missing: Head loss: film internal loss and bearing-edge friction are zero (no measured drum-head loss exists for this film). Entering any would shorten every T60, so these decays bound this model only

Upper-partial decay: part of the gap to the recording is the exterior formulation. In a 0.5 s test on the same binary, with the band cut to 320 Hz and (5,1) dropped so that plain CBIE can run, plain CBIE against closed-surface Burton-Miller lengthens (2,1) 1.25x, (1,2) about 1.4x and (3,1) about 2x, leaves (1,1) within 6 %, and lengthens (4,1) at least 2x, though that fit is unstable. It isn't all of the gap: (2,1) is still near 2.9 s and (3,1) near 5.5 s. The next suspect is the pole fit: (2,1) was 3.78 s on a 327-pole load and is 2.07 s on this 272-pole load, which is a correlation and not a cause. The render's T60s track the fit: in a 0.5 s test on a 234-pole plain CBIE load, not the published render's 272-pole load, they sit within 6 % of the fit's T60s on five lines, with (1,2) the exception, the fit's modal resistance on (1,1), (2,1), (3,1) and (4,1) is 2.5, 9.6, 30 and 114x the BEM values it fits on that load and 1.9, 2.1, 1.3 and 1.0x on the published Burton-Miller load, the two loads' BEM values disagree on the weak modes, and no fit has yet passed a 15 % limit on these lines

Upper-partial levels, a separate finding from decay: at 0.25 s the render's (2,1) to (5,1) sit 14, 31, 42 and 50 dB below (1,1), against 6, 20, 19 and 17 dB on one v5 hit of the recording, so 8 to 33 dB weak. The cause is not named, and the recording is another drum and mallet

Head modes above 380 Hz in vacuo ((1,3), (3,2), (6,1), (0,4) and higher): absent. Above the (5,1) pair, about 2.94 times the principal, the only partials are the kettle's air modes heard through the head (near 360, 550, 565, 690 and 730 Hz). The exterior load and the receiver transfer are fitted only from 40 to 400 Hz, so above 400 Hz those lines' levels and radiation damping are extrapolations

Duration: 4 s of one strike took 19.5 h; the exterior load's poles make each step cost about 50x the mechanics (pexfp.376.2). The file is 16-bit at 20 Pa full scale, so the signal ends between 2 and 3 s, (5,1)'s fit sits near that floor, and the last second is digital silence. render.sh can't write float32 until the kettle render does, which it has to before the next full render
The vent: the kettle is sealed
Kettle, stand and counterhoop are rigid and silent
Uniform tension: the degenerate pairs do not split, so there is no beating
Felt hysteresis: the mallet law is the source's hysteresis-free fit
Room: free field, no floor and no room decay
Converged interior air (illustrative numerical choice): the cavity cut at 1500 Hz leaves the coupled (2,1)..(5,1) ratios 0.5 to 1.1 % above a 2500 Hz basis (u-cavity-truncation; pexfp.376.1)
Converged head mesh (illustrative numerical choice): 6x48 puts the in-vacuo (2,1)..(5,1) ratios 0.3 to 1.6 % low (u-head-mesh)
